cls: Topical depigmenting agent (monobenzyl ether of hydroquinone)
pharm: The monobenzyl ether of hydroquinone applied topically; it is taken up by melanocytes where it interferes with melanin formation and produces selective, progressive, and PERMANENT destruction of melanocytes, leading to irreversible depigmentation of treated and sometimes distant skin.
quick: Apply 20% cream to affected (residually pigmented) areas 2-3 times daily
Use only if clearly needed; limited data on topical use
Use with caution; avoid application to areas of infant contact (e.g., breast)
Extent/uniformity of depigmentation, sun protection, satellite/distant depigmentation, dermatitis
summary: Monobenzone (monobenzyl ether of hydroquinone) is a topical depigmenting agent indicated ONLY for the FINAL depigmentation of normal pigmented skin remaining in patients with extensive vitiligo (vitiligo universalis). It causes PERMANENT, IRREVERSIBLE depigmentation by selectively destroying melanocytes, so it is fundamentally different from skin-lightening agents like hydroquinone. It is NOT a treatment for hyperpigmentation disorders such as melasma, freckles, or chloasma, and should never be used to lighten normally pigmented skin or for cosmetic bleaching. Depigmentation is unpredictable and may occur at sites distant from the application area (satellite/distant-site depigmentation). Because the result is permanent and patients become highly photosensitive, use requires careful counseling, lifelong sun protection, and the understanding that the change cannot be reversed.
indications: Final depigmentation of the normal pigmented skin that remains in patients with extensive (disseminated) vitiligo, to produce a more uniform skin color

dosage.d: Apply a thin layer to the residually pigmented areas to be depigmented
dosage.n: Depigmentation usually requires 1 to 4 months of regular use; satisfactory results may take up to a year

dosage.d: Apply as needed (often about twice weekly) to maintain depigmentation
dosage.n: Repigmentation can occur with sun exposure; ongoing sun protection and intermittent application may be needed

dosage.d: Do NOT use to treat melasma, freckles, chloasma, or to lighten normally pigmented skin
dosage.n: Indicated only for final depigmentation in extensive vitiligo; produces permanent, irreversible loss of pigment

admin: Apply a thin layer of 20% cream to the pigmented areas to be depigmented, 2 to 3 times daily; rub in well
Wash hands thoroughly after application unless the hands are being treated, to avoid depigmenting unintended areas
Avoid contact with the eyes and apply only to the intended skin
Test for sensitivity by applying to a small area for a few days before full use; discontinue if severe irritation, allergic contact dermatitis, or vesiculation occurs
Counsel the patient that the effect is permanent and irreversible and that response may take 1-4 months or longer
Emphasize strict, lifelong protection from sunlight (sunscreen, protective clothing) because depigmented skin burns easily and may repigment with sun exposure
moa: Monobenzone is the monobenzyl ether of hydroquinone. After topical application it is taken up by melanocytes, where it increases the formation of reactive oxygen species and acts as a substrate/competitive inhibitor in the melanin synthesis pathway. Unlike hydroquinone, which reversibly suppresses melanin production, monobenzone causes selective cytotoxicity to melanocytes, leading to their destruction and to a permanent, irreversible loss of pigment. Because melanocytes are destroyed rather than merely inhibited, the depigmentation does not resolve on stopping the drug, and an immune-mediated, spreading loss of pigment can occur at sites remote from the application area (satellite or distant-site depigmentation). The exact mechanism is not fully established.

absolute: Known hypersensitivity to monobenzone or any component
Use as a general skin-lightener or for hyperpigmentation disorders (e.g., melasma, freckles, chloasma) - not an indication
relative: Patients who do not understand or accept that the depigmentation is permanent and irreversible
Inability or unwillingness to maintain strict sun protection
monitor: Extent and uniformity of depigmentation in treated areas
Local irritation, erythema, burning, or allergic contact dermatitis
Adherence to sun protection and signs of sunburn in depigmented skin

preg: There are no adequate and well-controlled studies of topical monobenzone in pregnant women. It should be used during pregnancy only if clearly needed and after weighing the elective, cosmetic-functional nature of depigmentation against unknown fetal risk.
lact: It is not known whether topically applied monobenzone is excreted in human milk. Use with caution in nursing mothers; avoid application to the breast or to areas that may come into direct contact with the nursing infant.
renal: Not applicable - monobenzone is used topically; systemic absorption is limited and no renal dose adjustment is defined.
hepatic: Not applicable - monobenzone is used topically; systemic absorption is limited and no hepatic dose adjustment is defined.

minor: Other topical agents applied to the same area may alter absorption or local tolerability
interactions.alcohol: No clinically relevant interaction with systemic or topical alcohol.
interactions.diagnostics: No characteristic laboratory interference; the clinical endpoint is the degree of depigmentation.

common: Burning or stinging at the application site
serious: Permanent, irreversible depigmentation (the intended but unalterable effect)
Depigmentation at sites distant from application (satellite/distant-site depigmentation)
Severe photosensitivity of depigmented skin with risk of sunburn
rare: Contact eczema spreading beyond the treated area
emergency: Severe allergic contact dermatitis with widespread eruption

monitoring: Degree and uniformity of depigmentation in treated areas over weeks to months
Appearance of depigmentation at distant or untreated (satellite) sites
Local skin reactions - irritation, erythema, allergic contact dermatitis, vesiculation
Adherence to and adequacy of sun protection
Signs of sunburn in depigmented skin
counsel: This cream PERMANENTLY removes the remaining color from your skin - the change cannot be undone
It is used only to even out skin color when most of your skin has already lost pigment from extensive vitiligo
It is NOT a skin-bleaching cream for dark spots, melasma, or freckles, and should never be used for that
Color may also be lost in areas where you did not apply the cream - this is expected and is also permanent
Apply a thin layer 2 to 3 times a day and wash your hands afterward unless you are treating your hands
Results can take 1 to 4 months or longer to appear
Your treated skin will burn very easily in the sun - use strong sunscreen and protective clothing for life, every day
Stop and call your doctor if you get severe redness, blistering, or a spreading rash
pk: Visible depigmentation typically begins after several weeks of regular use
Maximal/uniform depigmentation usually over 1 to 4 months, sometimes up to a year
Not characterized for topical use; systemic absorption is minimal
Permanent and irreversible once melanocytes are destroyed
Store at controlled room temperature; keep tightly closed and protect from light
pearls: Causes PERMANENT, IRREVERSIBLE depigmentation by destroying melanocytes - fundamentally different from reversible lighteners like hydroquinone
Indicated ONLY for final depigmentation of residual normal skin in extensive vitiligo, to achieve uniform color
NEVER use for melasma, freckles, chloasma, or cosmetic skin lightening
Depigmentation can occur at distant/untreated (satellite) sites - counsel patients before starting
Depigmented skin is highly photosensitive - lifelong, strict sun protection is essential
Confirm the patient fully understands the permanent, unalterable nature before initiating; consider a sensitivity test patch
Repigmentation can occur with sun exposure, sometimes requiring maintenance applications
missed: If you miss an application, apply it as soon as you remember and then continue your usual schedule. Do not apply extra cream to make up for a missed application. Because the effect builds gradually, occasional missed applications are not dangerous, but consistent use gives the best result.
overdose: Monobenzone is for topical use only and should not be swallowed. If accidentally ingested, contact a poison control center; treatment is supportive. Excessive or prolonged topical application increases the extent of permanent depigmentation and the likelihood of irritation; discontinue and protect the skin from sun if marked or unwanted depigmentation or severe local reaction occurs.
